headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no direct shared channel is documented, but Argo’s API-driven workflows can still pass untrusted outputs into Spring samples if wired together.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between argo-workflows and spring-integration-samples, so direct injection is not evidenced. However, Argo can call APIs/GRPC and Spring Integration samples are integration-oriented, so a manual or orchestrated bridge could pass attacker-controlled content. The pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF an operator wires Argo outputs into Spring Integration message handlers or file inputs
IF untrusted content is copied from one agent’s output into the other’s control path
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Add explicit content validation before any handoff
Use a provenance tag on all inter-agent messages
Disable any automatic parsing of peer outputs
requires-engineering: add a broker that strips instructions from payloads

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo-workflows touches artifacts and parameters and has allowlisted egress, while spring-integration-samples reports no data classes touched and no egress. That makes broad leakage unlikely, but if shared files or parameters contain sensitive data, Argo could transmit them through its outbound allowlist. The pairwise risk is limited and not default.
conditions: IF sensitive artifacts or parameters are placed in a shared workspace
IF Argo is configured to send those artifacts to an allowlisted external endpoint
mitigations: Store sensitive inputs outside any shared directory
Review Argo allowlist destinations before execution
Remove secrets from parameters and artifacts
Use separate service accounts for each agent
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on outbound artifact uploads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo-workflows exposes API calls and allowlisted egress, but spring-integration-samples has no write, network, or OAuth scopes documented. With no overlapping mutable resource or shared write surface, a capability conflict is not supported by the profiles. Uncertainty does not increase severity here because the missing write surface blocks the main pathway.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples is later granted write access to the same mutable resource as Argo
IF both agents are deployed under a shared lockless workspace
mitigations: Keep mutable resources separate
Avoid granting overlapping scopes
Document ownership of each API target
Use per-agent credentials
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo can produce workflow artifacts and parameters, and Spring Integration samples are designed for message-flow composition, so one agent’s output could be consumed by the other. But there is no evidence that spring-integration-samples treats Argo output as authoritative or takes downstream actions by default, so the cascade is plausible but not demonstrated.
conditions: IF Argo-generated artifacts are fed directly into Spring Integration flows
IF the Spring flow acts on those inputs without validation
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents
Require schema validation on all handoffs
Log and review the first few exchanged messages
Mark Argo outputs as untrusted by default
requires-engineering: add automated cross-checks before actions

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either argo-workflows or spring-integration-samples. Both profiles are open-source docs-only entries with no sensitive data classes or compliance claims, so a compliance breach pathway is not established from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF either agent is later deployed in a regulated environment with stricter residency or retention rules
IF sensitive regulated data is introduced into the workflow
mitigations: Record the data classes before deployment
Check residency requirements for any hosted backend
Avoid placing regulated data in sample integrations
Use separate retention policies per system
requires-engineering: add compliance policy enforcement
